hero_image.prompt: Premium robotics textbook illustration of RoboRover, a small wheeled educational rover, following a black line on a light laboratory floor. Show the rover slightly to the right of the line with a subtle leftward correction arrow, sensor beams aimed at the line, and a clean visual suggestion of repeated measure-compare-correct behavior. Technically plausible wheels, line sensors, chassis, restrained modern editorial styling, realistic materials and lighting, no decorative sci-fi elements, minimal labels.
hero_image.caption: RoboRover measures its position relative to the line and corrects its motion instead of relying on one fixed command.
hero_image.alt_text: Small wheeled RoboRover positioned to the right of a black floor line, with sensors observing the line and a leftward correction arrow.

inline_visuals.prompt: Clean technical control-loop diagram for a beginner robotics textbook. Show four labeled stages arranged in a loop: desired position, compare with sensor measurement, choose correction, robot motion. Use arrows to show the measurement returning from the robot to the comparison stage. Include a small line-following RoboRover icon and clearly distinguish desired state, measured state, error, and correction. Professional vector-style engineering diagram, restrained colors, high visual clarity, minimal text.
inline_visuals.caption: Feedback sends information about the robot's measured result back into its next control decision.
inline_visuals.alt_text: A four-stage circular feedback diagram connecting desired position, comparison, correction choice, robot motion, and sensor measurement.

inline_visuals.prompt: Educational sequential diagram showing RoboRover correcting lateral position relative to a straight black line. Three panels: first the rover is 6 centimeters right of the line with a large left arrow, second it is 3 centimeters right with a smaller left arrow, third it is close to the line with a tiny correction or straight motion. Use a clean floor coordinate convention with right positive and left negative, limited essential labels, premium robotics textbook styling.
inline_visuals.caption: Repeated measurements let the correction become smaller as RoboRover approaches the desired line.
inline_visuals.alt_text: Three-panel sequence of RoboRover moving from far right of a line toward the line with progressively smaller correction arrows.

inline_visuals.prompt: Technically plausible close-up engineering illustration of RoboRover's line-following sensors and lateral position. Show a straight black tape line on a pale floor, the rover center offset to the right, sensor footprint near the line, a coordinate marker at the desired center, and a clear leftward correction arrow. Include subtle measurement annotations for 6.0 centimeters and 2.0 centimeter deadband without making the image text-heavy. Premium robotics educational editorial style, realistic materials and lighting.
inline_visuals.caption: The signed error identifies both how far RoboRover is from the line and which direction the correction should take.
inline_visuals.alt_text: RoboRover offset to the right of a floor line, with sensor measurement, desired center marker, deadband region, and leftward correction arrow.

inline_visuals.prompt: Clean educational visualization of a discrete feedback simulation: a horizontal position axis centered on a target line at zero centimeters, a sequence of RoboRover positions moving from plus 6 centimeters toward plus 1.2 centimeters, small alternating sensor-noise markers, and arrows indicating repeated left corrections followed by straight motion inside a deadband. Professional technical textbook graphic, restrained palette, no clutter, labels only where essential.
inline_visuals.caption: The simulation records actual position, noisy measured position, error, and the selected action at every feedback step.
inline_visuals.alt_text: Technical diagram showing simulated RoboRover positions approaching a zero-centimeter target while measurements include small noise and corrections stop inside a deadband.
